# quantms Pipeline — Full Reference

> Cloud-ready Nextflow pipeline for DDA quantitative proteomics (LFQ and TMT/iTRAQ). Published in Nature Methods 2024.

## Overview

quantms is a Nextflow pipeline that takes raw mass spectrometry data, an SDRF sample metadata file, and a protein FASTA database, and produces identified and quantified proteins. It supports two main workflows:

1. Label-Free Quantification (LFQ): Raw files → file conversion (ThermoRawFileParser) → decoy database generation (DecoyPYrat) → database search (Comet + MS-GF+ + Sage in parallel) → PSM feature generation (MS2Rescore) → FDR control (Percolator) → consensus identification (ConsensusID) → protein-level FDR → quantification (ProteomicsLFQ) → MSstats export → QC report (pmultiqc)

2. Isobaric Labeling (TMT/iTRAQ): Same identification pipeline, then IsobaricAnalyzer for reporter ion extraction → protein quantification → MSstats export → QC report

## Installation

### Prerequisites
- Nextflow >= 21.10.3
- Container runtime: Docker (recommended), Singularity, or Conda

### Run with Docker
nextflow run bigbio/quantms -r main -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --database proteins.fasta \
  --outdir results/

### Run with Singularity (HPC)
nextflow run bigbio/quantms -r main -profile singularity \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --database proteins.fasta \
  --outdir results/

## Input Files

### Samplesheet (CSV)
spectra_file,sdrf_file
/path/to/sample1.raw,/path/to/sdrf.tsv
/path/to/sample2.raw,/path/to/sdrf.tsv

### SDRF File
Tab-separated file following the SDRF-Proteomics standard. Defines sample metadata, experimental design, and analysis parameters. Download from PRIDE for public datasets or create with sdrf-pipelines.

Key SDRF columns:
- source name: sample identifier
- characteristics[organism]: species (e.g., Homo sapiens)
- characteristics[disease]: condition (e.g., normal, cancer)
- comment[instrument]: mass spectrometer model
- comment[modification parameters]: PTMs to search
- comment[precursor mass tolerance]: search tolerance
- comment[fragment mass tolerance]: fragment tolerance

### FASTA Database
Standard UniProt FASTA format. Decoy sequences are generated automatically by the pipeline using DecoyPYrat.

## Key Parameters

### Search Engines
- --search_engines comet,msgf,sage (default: all three)
- Results are merged via ConsensusID (at least 2 engines must agree)

### FDR Thresholds
- --fdr_level peptide_level_fdrs or protein_level_fdrs
- --psm_level_fdr_cutoff 0.01 (default: 1% PSM FDR)
- --peptide_level_fdr_cutoff 0.01 (default: 1% peptide FDR)
- --protein_level_fdr_cutoff 0.01 (default: 1% protein FDR)

### Rescoring
- --posterior_eval_fdr 0.01
- --rescoring_engine ms2rescore (default)
- Features: DeepLC retention time, MS2PIP fragmentation, basic PSM features

### LFQ-Specific
- --labelling_type label free sample
- --quantification_method feature_intensity
- --targeted_only true (only quantify identified peptides)

### TMT/iTRAQ-Specific
- --labelling_type tmt or --labelling_type itraq
- --iso_activation HCD (or CID, ETD)
- --reference_channel (for ratio calculation)

## Output Files

results/
├── mztab/                    # mzTab identification results
├── idxml/                    # OpenMS idXML files
├── consensusxml/             # Consensus features
├── msstats/                  # MSstats input CSV
│   └── msstats_input.csv     # Ready for MSstats R package
├── pmultiqc/                 # QC report
│   └── multiqc_report.html   # Interactive HTML report
└── pipeline_info/            # Nextflow execution reports

### MSstats Export
The pipeline exports an MSstats-compatible CSV for downstream statistical analysis. This is NOT a processing step — it produces input for the MSstats R package.

## Common Workflows

### Reanalyze a PRIDE dataset
# 1. Get SDRF from PRIDE
wget https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/pride/resources/proteomes/sdrf/PXD000001.sdrf.tsv
# 2. Download raw files listed in SDRF
# 3. Create samplesheet CSV pointing to files + SDRF
# 4. Run pipeline
nextflow run bigbio/quantms -r main -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --database uniprot_human.fasta \
  --outdir PXD000001_results/

### LFQ analysis with custom parameters
nextflow run bigbio/quantms -r main -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --database proteins.fasta \
  --search_engines comet,sage \
  --psm_level_fdr_cutoff 0.01 \
  --protein_level_fdr_cutoff 0.01 \
  --outdir results/

### TMT analysis
nextflow run bigbio/quantms -r main -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --database proteins.fasta \
  --labelling_type tmt \
  --iso_activation HCD \
  --outdir results/

## Integration with Ecosystem

- Input metadata: SDRF files (sdrf-pipelines for validation)
- QC reports: pmultiqc generates interactive HTML reports from quantms output
- Downstream quantification: mokume can process quantms peptide-level output for iBAQ, TopN, etc.
- Data format: qpx converts quantms output to standardized QPX Parquet format
- Reanalyzed data: quantms Portal hosts 251 datasets processed with quantms

## Troubleshooting

- Pipeline hangs at database search: increase memory with --max_memory 32.GB
- No proteins identified: check SDRF organism matches FASTA database species
- TMT missing channels: verify SDRF comment[label] matches your labeling scheme
- Docker permission errors: run with --profile singularity on shared HPC

## Related Tools

- quantmsdiann: DIA proteomics pipeline (https://quantmsdiann.quantms.org)
- pmultiqc: QC reports plugin (https://pmultiqc.quantms.org)
- mokume: protein quantification library (https://mokume.quantms.org)
- qpx: data format toolkit (https://qpx.quantms.org)
- quantms Portal: data portal (https://portal.quantms.org)

## Citation

Dai C et al. quantms: a cloud-based pipeline for quantitative proteomics enables the reanalysis of public proteomics data. Nature Methods. 2024;21:1603-1607. DOI: 10.1038/s41592-024-02343-1
